subject_name: Aircraft Electrical equipment, Power generation and Distribution
topic: Principle of operation and constructional details of rotational speed measurement
syllabus_extract: Principle of operation and constructional details of rotational speed measurement. Principle of operation and constructional details. Practical on rotational speed measurement.
specific_objectives: 15.1.6.1 Trainee will be able to explain construction and working of RPM indicator.

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Demonstration of RPM indicator calibration and reading verification; Safety: Ensure generator is de-energized before handling; Instructor supervision: Monitor trainee interaction with measurement instruments.
intro_questions: What is the function of the RPM indicator in an aircraft?
Where is the RPM indicator typically located in the cockpit?
Why is accurate rotational speed measurement critical for engine operation?

topics: Basic principle of rotational speed measurement
development.content:
Basic principle of rotational speed measurement
Construction details of RPM indicator
Working mechanism of generator excitation
Signal transmission to cockpit display
Calibration and zeroing procedures

Detailed analysis of sensor types
Interpretation of tachometer signals
Troubleshooting common faults
Impact of temperature on readings
Maintenance requirements for sensors

topics: Comparison of theoretical vs actual values
development.content:
Hands-on demonstration of RPM measurement
Verification of indicator accuracy
Recording of practical observations
Comparison of theoretical vs actual values
Documentation of practical findings

summary_questions: Explain the working principle of the RPM indicator in your own words.
Describe the constructional details of the RPM indicator and its components.
How would you troubleshoot a faulty RPM indicator reading?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief report on the differences between the RPM indicator discussed in this lesson and the electrical tachometer system to be covered in LP 15.
